title: Low-level laser therapy
what: A specialist aims a weak laser beam at the sore area. It does not cut or burn. It helps the tissues heal.
why: For joint and muscle pain, after injuries, and for slow-healing wounds, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: a session usually takes 5 to 15 minutes; a course is usually about 10 sessions
tell_doctor: Moles or growths in that area
If you take medicines that make you sensitive to light

prepare.title: Skin
prepare.text: Skin should be clean, with no cream or makeup in the area.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that lets you uncover the area.

steps: You may be given protective glasses
The probe is placed on the skin or held close to it
The device works for a few minutes on each spot
The session ends at the signal
after: You can return to normal activities right away
Avoid sunbathing in the first days of the course. Check with your doctor
Come to sessions on schedule. The full course matters
red_flags: A burn or strong redness in the treated area: show your doctor

faq.q: Is the laser dangerous for the eyes?
faq.a: You must not look at the beam, so you get glasses. For the skin, this laser is safe.
No. Usually you feel nothing, or just mild warmth.

reminders.text: Laser therapy today. No cream on your skin. Bring your referral.
